title: Delete the dead onCompleted callback chain from DailyTaskCard/GroupedDailyView/SchedulerScreen

evidence.quote:
onDismissed: () => onTaskDismissed(curriculum, i),
              onCompleted: () => onTaskCompleted(curriculum, i),

why: DailyTaskCard.onCompleted is `required` (every caller must supply it) but nothing inside DailyTaskCard ever invokes `onCompleted()` — its own doc comment even admits 'Kept for call-site compatibility; invoked externally', but no external invocation exists either. The real completion-triggered refresh path is `completionCommittedProvider`, incremented by text_display_screen.dart:696 and watched by allDailyTasksProvider (scheduler_providers.dart:321) — a reactive mechanism unrelated to this callback. daily_task_card_test.dart confirms this: every test passes `onCompleted: () {}` and none assert it fires. The whole chain (DailyTaskCard's param, SchedulerScreen._TaskList's and GroupedDailyView-wiring's invalidate closures, GroupedDailyView's pass-through) is vestigial from a pre-completionCommittedProvider design.
recommendation: Remove the onCompleted parameter from DailyTaskCard and GroupedDailyView, and the corresponding dead closures in scheduler_screen.dart.
acceptance_criteria: DailyTaskCard and GroupedDailyView no longer declare onCompleted/onTaskCompleted.
daily_task_card_test.dart and scheduler_screen tests updated accordingly and still pass.
